title: A laser show on Paranal
caption: Laser beams and star trails above the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Long arcs of starlight curve across the sky above ESO's Paranal Observatory in this photograph, taken over several hours. Beams of orange light burst from one of the Unit Telescopes, and a smaller Auxiliary Telescope sits in the foreground on the right.

The Very Large Telescope combines four big Unit Telescopes with four smaller Auxiliary Telescopes that can be moved around. The orange beams come from the Four Laser Guide Star Facility, which sets sodium atoms high in the atmosphere glowing as artificial stars. The twinkling of those artificial stars is measured in real time, and the adaptive optics system uses it to undo the atmosphere's blurring so the telescope can take sharp images.

Each laser delivers 22 watts, roughly 4000 times the legal limit for a laser pointer, and its beam is about 30 centimeters wide. The beams point in opposite directions only because, during the hours-long exposure, the telescope moved to observe different targets.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph built up over several hours at ESO's Paranal Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye would see stars as points and one set of beams at a time. The hours-long exposure records the star trails and beams pointing in different directions together.
